summary.intent: Improve memory quality in the memory-loop system by enforcing a hard evidence gate on generated memory records, and fix the summary command's slow first load.
summary.outcome: Implemented a two-layer evidence gate (provenance + session ID validation) replacing the weak review-derived gate, added FilteredNoEvidenceCount stat, fixed JSON parsing for LLM trailing text, and removed unconditional backfill from the summary command startup.

repo: AffectedSessions in PatternAnalysis uses CheckpointID, but the prompt was previously exposing SessionID — identifier alignment is a prerequisite for cross-referencing generated memories against analysis signals.
passesReviewDerivedGate (generator.go:360) was the only hard gate before this change; all other kinds (repo_rule, workflow_rule, agent_instruction) only had soft LLM-instruction-based filtering.
The summary command ran BackfillSummaries and BackfillFacets unconditionally on every invocation (summary_cmd.go:195-196), causing 20+ sequential LLM calls with output to io.Discard on first load.
repo_learning and workflow_learning signals have no Count or AffectedSessions fields, making them ineligible as provenance sources for the evidence gate.
llmcli.ExtractJSONFromMarkdown strips markdown code fences but does not strip trailing natural-language text after a closing brace, causing json.Unmarshal failures.
Personal-scope memory records auto-activate without TUI promotion (memoryloop.go:623), so Option 4 (TUI evidence display) does not protect the most common injection path.

code.finding: Prompt instruction 'Avoid one-off incidents without repeated evidence' was the only enforcement — a suggestion to the LLM, not a code gate.
Post-filter caught low confidence and low strength but a one-off record with confidence:high and strength:4 passed through.
SourceSessionIDs was captured but never validated for length; a single-session record was treated identically to a 5-session one.
passesReviewDerivedGate enforced count>=2 || strong only for review-derived rules; replaced by passesEvidenceGate which covers all signal types.
Unconditional backfill calls on every summary command invocation caused 50-170s silent startup; removed so backfill only runs on explicit user request.

workflow: Using Codex as a second reviewer on architecture docs before implementation caught two critical flaws: missing provenance data model and a fallback-allows escape hatch that nullified the gate.
Writing an analysis doc and iterating it with a second AI reviewer before implementing is effective for catching architectural gaps early.
Rebuild the CLI binary after committing fixes — the error recurred because the old binary was still running.

friction: LLM returned trailing text after JSON closing brace ('invalid character n after top-level value'), requiring an extractJSONObject fallback parser.
After committing the JSON fix, the error recurred because the CLI binary wasn't rebuilt — wasted a debug cycle.
Many existing tests had to be updated to include SourceSignal + analysis signals + valid SourceSessionIDs after the evidence gate was added, requiring careful reading of 12+ test cases.
identifier alignment (SessionID vs CheckpointID) was a prerequisite blocker that had to be resolved before Layer 2 validation could work correctly.
logicalRuleSimilarity was defined in memoryloop.go and used there independently, requiring careful scoping when removing the review gate helpers.
open_items: Option 4 (show evidence count in TUI before promotion) was noted as still useful for transparency alongside the evidence gate, but not implemented.
Existing low-quality memories already in memory-loop.json are not affected by the evidence gate — a backfill/re-evaluation pass or natural decay would be needed to clean them up.
improve/generator.go and facets/facets.go may have the same trailing-text JSON parsing issue as memoryloop/generator.go — not investigated.
A new GenerationStats counter FilteredNoEvidenceCount was added but the doc noted it would be useful for debugging — actual observability of the new gate in production is unverified.
The matchedSignal.Kind refinement (line 220 in doc) prevents singleton exceptions from leaking across signal types — noted but implementation details not fully verified in transcript.
